ARTEFACT: Movable archaeological finds of every kind and groups of finds recovered in archaeological contexts. This includes pottery and ceramic assemblages, tools, jewellery, figurines, seals, inscriptions, clothing items, and objects depicted on artefacts or works of art, architectural members when treated as finds, bones, deposited remains, and parts of artefacts such as «λαβές». Annotate the core artefact noun, not descriptive adjectives unless they form a fixed artefact type or are necessary to identify the object. Examples: «ενώτια», «αλιευτικά δίχτυα». Include the full artefact phrase when the modifier is part of the object name or meaning, e.g. «σκύφου μὲ δακτυλιόσχημη βάση». Do not annotate immovable structures such as tombs, walls, temples, altars, stoas, or acropoleis as ARTEFACT.
PERIOD: Archaeological periods, chronological phases, cultural phases, and ancient date ranges. Include the full chronological expression, including modifiers and prepositions such as «από» when they are part of a date range. For chronological ranges, annotate the entire range as one PERIOD span, not the individual dates separately. Examples: «Νεολιθική εποχή», «Τελική Νεολιθική», «πρωιμότερη της Πρώιμης Εποχής του Χαλκού», «παλαιότερες τῆς Νεολιθικῆς περιόδους», «κατὰ τὴν ἀρχαιότερη φάση», «ΥΕ ΙΙΙΒ/Γ», «από το 3600 ως το 3000 π.Χ.», «από τον 8ο αι. π.Χ. μέχρι τον 2ο αι. μ.Χ.», «από τον 2ο αι. π.Χ. έως το 69 π.Χ.», «από το 15ο αι. π.Χ. και μετά». Exclude modern dates, excavation seasons, and modern historical references.
LOCATION: Named geographical places and place names, including cities, villages, regions, countries, islands, ancient place names, museums, and named archaeological sites when used primarily as toponyms rather than structures. Include complete place-name expressions, especially when they contain personal-name elements, saints' names, genitives, or regional qualifiers. Examples: «Πλωτινόπολη», «Ραμνοῦς», «Ραμνοῦντος», «Δήλος», «Θεολόγος Θάσου», «Άγιος Ιωάννης Λουκάς Θεολόγου», «όρμος του Αγίου Ιωάννη». Do not classify saint-based or person-like place names as PERSON when the expression denotes a place. Do not annotate generic geographical nouns alone, such as «νησί», «πλαγιά», or «θέση», unless they are part of a named place expression.
CONTEXT: Immovable archaeological contexts, built spaces, architectural structures, and in situ parts of structures. This includes temples, sanctuaries, altars, stoas, agoras, acropoleis, cemeteries, deposits, ruins, architectural spaces, and structural architectural members when they are part of a building or monument. Prefer the complete meaningful structure span, especially when an adjective or genitive identifies the structure. Examples: «βωμός», «πηγάδι», «ελλειψοειδείς οικίες», «ἀκρόπολη», «Ιερό του Απόλλωνα», «Ιερό», «ἱεροῦ της Ἀφροδίτης Ἡγεμόνης», «Ιερό του Πανός», «θεμέλια τοίχου», «παραστάδες», «επιστύλιο», «γείσο». Do not annotate generic functional expressions such as «λατρευτικό κέντρο» as CONTEXT. Do not annotate loose fills or surface deposits such as «ἐπιχώσεις» as CONTEXT unless they are explicitly treated as an archaeological layer or deposit. Do not annotate named geographical places as CONTEXT.
MATERIAL: Specific materials, substances, animal-derived materials, pigments, and material adjectives from which artefacts, structures, or finds are made. Examples: «μάρμαρο», «λίθος», «λίθινα», «πηλός», «άργιλος», «χαλκός», «χρυσός». Annotate material adjectives separately from artefacts when they simply indicate material, e.g. «πήλινων» + «βαριδίων» or «χρυσός» + «σόλιδος». Do not annotate material words when they are part of a PERIOD expression, e.g. «Χαλκού» in «Πρώιμη Εποχή του Χαλκού». Do not annotate broad generic expressions such as «πρώτες ύλες» unless a specific material is named. If bones, ceramics, or fragments are described as deposited finds rather than as the substance of another object, annotate them as ARTEFACT instead of MATERIAL.
SPECIES: Animal and plant species, including real, symbolic, and mythological animals when they denote living beings or depicted creatures. Include parenthetical or synonymous species terms when present. Examples: «λιοντάρι», «λιονταράκι», «σκύμνος», «φίδι», «γρύπας». If the animal or plant term denotes the material of an object, such as shell or bone, annotate it as MATERIAL instead of SPECIES. Do not annotate personal names, divine figures, or mythological persons as SPECIES.
PERSON: Historical, mythological, divine, religious, or legendary figures mentioned as persons or named beings. Examples: «Αλέξανδρος», «Αλέξανδρος ο Μέγας», «Απόλλων», «Απόλλωνα», «Ρωμανού Β΄», «Κωνσταντίνου Ζ΄ Πορφυρογέννητου». Include numerals, ordinal markers, epithets, and titles when they are part of the personal name, e.g. «IV», «Β΄», «Πορφυρογέννητος». Exclude modern archaeologists, researchers, authors, excavators, and scholars. Do not annotate personal-name elements as PERSON when they are part of a place name, such as «Θεολόγος Θάσου».
FEATURE: Stylistic, typological, iconographic, decorative, technical, morphological, or formal characteristics of artefacts, figures, or artistic representations. Annotate features when they describe decoration, technique, or iconography, but do not over-annotate ordinary descriptive adjectives unless they are part of the annotation guidelines. Examples: «διάτρητες», «εμπίεση», «ανάγλυφη διακόσμηση», «ανθρωπόμορφα», «ζωόμορφα», «ένθρονη μορφή», «ερυθρόμορφο». Do not annotate simple shape adjectives such as «σφαιρικές», «επιμήκεις», or isolated adjectives as FEATURE unless the guidelines explicitly treat them as independent features. Do not split a complete artefact expression into FEATURE + ARTEFACT when the modifier is part of the artefact span, e.g. annotate «πατριαρχικό σταυρό» as ARTEFACT, not «πατριαρχικό» as FEATURE plus «σταυρό» as ARTEFACT.
